title: OpenAI disbands its robotics team as its general models start running robots
lede: Fortune reports OpenAI has broken up its stand-alone robotics team, moving researchers into core research and hardware staff into Applied, because its general models now control robots directly.

points: Robotics research now reports to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen; applied robotics and hardware moved under President Greg Brockman.
OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra proved usable for robotics without a dedicated model, replacing an earlier plan to build on Sora.
In an Nvidia study, an Astra-driven agent scored 74.8% on a simulated manipulation benchmark against 51.0% for the best specialist models.
The move comes as OpenAI cuts side projects and losses ahead of a possible early-2027 IPO; it still targets a humanoid demo in 2027.
Robotics founders counter that deployment data from real sites and small on-board models still matter, since cloud LLMs are slow.

points.text: The top comment says general models run robots badly; millisecond control needs fast, smaller models, with a large model only planning.
Others read it as the Bitter Lesson again: general scale beats specialised systems.
Commenters split on whether it is pre-IPO cost cutting; a reply notes the researchers were moved, not laid off.
Several ask about the latency and token cost of streaming commands, and whether robots without a cloud link are still in scope.
